statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-42257 (GHSA-hm49-wcqc-g2xg): in the Ruby net-imap gem, several Net::IMAP commands pass caller-supplied strings to the server as raw protocol data without validating them, so an application that forwards untrusted input can be made to send additional IMAP commands (command injection): https://github.com/ruby/net-imap/security/advisories/GHSA-hm49-wcqc-g2xg. Upstream fixed it in net-imap 0.4.24 on the 0.4 line, 0.5.14 on the 0.5 line and 0.6.4 on the 0.6 line; the 0.6.4 release notes list GHSA-hm49-wcqc-g2xg: https://github.com/ruby/net-imap/releases/tag/v0.6.4. The DHI ruby-4.0 package for Alpine 3.23 is published as 4.0.1-r0, 4.0.1-r1, 4.0.2-r1, 4.0.2-r2, 4.0.3-r2, 4.0.4-r2, 4.0.4-r3, 4.0.5-r3, 4.0.6-r3, 4.0.6-r4, 4.0.7-r4, 4.0.9-r4, 4.0.10-r4 and 4.0.10-r5, for x86_64 and aarch64. It ships net-imap in its ruby4.0-net-imap gem package, which carries the gem's version rather than Ruby's, so the range below is written in the ruby-4.0 package's own versions, and each ruby-4.0 build is placed by the net-imap its ruby4.0-net-imap package installs. The gem package keeps the gem's own version but takes its -rN release number from the Ruby build that produced it, and the repository keeps one copy of each package version, so the gem package versions published under a given -rN are exactly the net-imap releases the Ruby builds with that -rN shipped. We read Net::IMAP::VERSION in lib/net/imap.rb of every published ruby4.0-net-imap package for both architectures, each verified against the repository index checksum, and listed the contents of every published ruby-4.0-libs package: the published ruby4.0-net-imap packages are 0.6.2-r0, 0.6.2-r1, 0.6.2-r2, 0.6.2-r3, 0.6.4.1-r3, 0.6.4.1-r4 and 0.6.4.1-r5. 0.6.2-r0, -r1 and -r2 install net-imap 0.6.2, the only gem version under -r0, -r1 and -r2, so 4.0.1-r0 through 4.0.4-r2 ship 0.6.2. Under -r3 two gem versions exist: 0.6.2-r3, which despite its label installs net-imap 0.6.4, and 0.6.4.1-r3, which installs net-imap 0.6.4.1. The 4.0.4-r3 and 4.0.5-r3 builds are the ones that replaced their bundled net-imap with 0.6.4: ruby-4.0-libs 4.0.4-r3 and 4.0.5-r3 both carry the net-imap-0.6.4 gem archive that install left behind, while no other ruby-4.0-libs build carries a net-imap archive; 4.0.6-r3 ships 0.6.4.1. 0.6.4.1-r4 and 0.6.4.1-r5 install net-imap 0.6.4.1, so 4.0.6-r4, 4.0.7-r4, 4.0.9-r4, 4.0.10-r4 and 4.0.10-r5 ship 0.6.4.1. Both architectures agree for every build. Every ruby-4.0 build before 4.0.4-r3 ships a net-imap without this fix, and 4.0.4-r3 is the first that ships net-imap 0.6.4, so the range is introduced at the first published build and fixed at 4.0.4-r3.
